To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription factors c-myc and max regulate the expression of genes involved in response to ART in human colon, ovarian and lung cancer cell lines.

ART exerts cytotoxic effects towards human cancer cells by affecting the expression of genes involved in ribosome biogenesis, cellular antioxidant defense and apoptosis, and that c-Myc/ Max-mediated transcriptional regulation might be a key mechanism for ART to exert cytotoxic effects towards cancer cells.

ART exerts its cytotoxic effects in cancer cells via the c-Myc/ Max transcriptional complex and that this complex regulates genes that are involved and not involved in the response of tumor cells to ART.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of ART-regulated genes and the elucidation of the transcriptional mechanisms underlying their expression.
the identification of ART-regulated genes and the elucidation of their underlying signaling pathways.
identification of novel targets for ART and development of novel therapy strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ART influences a wide range of cellular processes, which may explain the broad spectrum of therapeutic effects of ART, including its cytotoxic activity towards tumor cells.
the cytotoxic activity and the cytotoxicity of ART towards human colon, ovarian and lung cancer cell lines are associated with a complex network of gene expression changes.
the cytotoxic activity and the side effects of ART are mediated by c-Myc/ Max-regulated genes, whose transcriptional regulation is modulated by ART.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ART is an interesting candidate drug for treatment of tumors, which is associated with the transcription factors c-myc and max.
ART exerts its cytotoxic activity by affecting the expression of a set of genes.
ART is a multi-target drug, which exerts its cytotoxic activity by affecting a variety of signaling pathways, which are regulated by c-Myc and/or Max.
The main takeaway from our work is that
c-Myc/Myb-regulated gene expression might contribute significantly to the therapeutic efficacy of ART in cancer therapy.
the cytotoxic activity towards tumor cells is not only dependent on the activity of a single gene or a single signaling pathway, but rather a complex interplay of multiple factors.
c-Myc/ Max-regulated gene expression may be involved in the cytotoxic activity, but also in the side effects of ART.
